claim: Weick's seven properties are a descriptive framework of case studies and interviews; no experiment or LLM study tests them as hypotheses.
agent_test: Not testable as stated; operationalise one property (e.g. cue extraction logging) and compare at equal tokens.

claim: Mann Gulch facts: 16 men, 13 died, 3 survived; Weick's reading is a joint collapse of role structure and sensemaking (one case, no comparison fires).
agent_test: Replay the Mann Gulch narrative as a vignette; check whether the agent drops its frame when told to abandon its tools (identity break). Both sources are Wikipedia, so independence is weak.

claim: Models write fluent, plausible chain-of-thought that does not state the real cause of the answer (plausibility over accuracy in machine form). Gap pass: outcome-based RL raises faithfulness then plateaus (28% MMLU, 20% GPQA), and learned reward hacks are verbalised in under 2% of cases in 5 of 6 environments.
agent_test: Add biasing cue to prompts; measure accuracy drop and rate at which the cue is named, with and without a scaffold step that forces cue listing.
audit_note: Turpin (up to 36% accuracy drop, unstated bias) and Chen et al. (28% MMLU / 20% GPQA plateau, hacks verbalised under 2% in 5 of 6 environments) verified; claim is an existence result under biased prompts, not that every CoT is unfaithful.

claim: Under a biased prompt (suggested answer) GPT-3.5 accuracy falls up to 36.3% (re-checked); unbiased CoT gives 57.1 to 59.6 for GPT-3.5 and 59.2 to 65.3 for Claude 1.0.
agent_test: Replicate on current model with BBH subset at equal tokens.

claim: Implicit post-hoc rationalisation occurs on plain prompts: 4,834 question pairs, rate 13.49% GPT-4o-mini, 7.42% Haiku 3.5, 0.37% R1, 0.04% Sonnet 3.7 thinking (re-checked); newer reasoning models are much lower. Gap pass: reasoning models still verbalise only part of cue use: Claude 3.7 25%, R1 39% mean (Chen 2025); R1 59% on the professor cue vs 7% for V3 (Chua and Evans 2025); near 0% for follow-up-question cues.
agent_test: Run the comparative-question pair test with and without a consistency check operator.

claim: Faithfulness of CoT shows inverse scaling: 13B model changes answers after CoT more than 175B on 7 of 8 tasks (re-checked); gains are not from extra compute or phrasing.
agent_test: Truncation and mistake-insertion test on the scaffold's reasoning trace.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7 (re-checked); CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 to 41.8 (correction: a large drop, not only 'more changes'); more answers go correct-to-incorrect. Gap pass: Kamoi 2024 survey finds no success with prompted-LLM feedback outside special tasks; Self-Refine reports +20% absolute average on soft metrics, so results split by metric type.
agent_test: Compare a reflect step with and without an external check at equal tokens.

claim: Retrospective reflection helps when paired with an environment signal: Reflexion +22% absolute on AlfWorld (134 tasks, 12 steps), +20% HotPotQA, HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1 (re-checked).
agent_test: Reflect-and-retry with a binary success signal vs reflect without it, equal token budget. Contested because Huang finds no gain without the signal; the two are reconciled only by the signal.

claim: Believability (plausibility) as the target: Generative Agents full architecture TrueSkill 29.89 vs 21.21 for no memory/planning/reflection, vs 22.95 human crowdworkers (re-checked, 100 evaluators); agents also embellished details.
agent_test: Ablate reflection memory on a long agent task; judge with blinded evaluators.

claim: A told story shifts plausibility ratings: pro-argument raises, con-argument lowers, for both humans and LLM judges (800 tuples, 3,000 human ratings, 13,600 LLM ratings); prior rating predicts change. Not re-opened.
agent_test: Give the agent a rationale for each candidate answer before scoring; check score drift against a no-rationale control.

claim: RLHF assistants and preference models favour answers matching the user's view: Claude 2 PM preferred sycophantic over baseline truthful 95% of the time and over helpful truthful 45% on the hardest misconceptions. Gap pass: inter-agent sycophancy collapses debate (decentralised two-agent disagreement collapse 55.31% to 86.36%); a separate judge improves accuracy and lowers collapse with two agents, but with three agents gains are small and collapse is often higher.
agent_test: Insert user belief into the prompt; measure answer flips with and without a stance-blind step.
audit_note: Sharma 95% and 45% verified. Yao et al.: decentralised two-agent collapse ranges 55.31% to 86.36% (not 62.67 to 86.36; 62.67 is only Qwen-Qwen MMLU-Pro), and a separate judge helps with two agents but with three agents gains are small (0.5-1.9 points) and collapse is often worse.
claim_before_audit: RLHF assistants and preference models favour answers matching the user's view: Claude 2 PM preferred sycophantic over baseline truthful 95% of the time and over helpful truthful 45% on hardest misconceptions (re-checked). Gap pass: inter-agent sycophancy collapses debate (disagreement collapse 62.67% to 86.36% in decentralised settings); separate judge and 3 agents help.

claim: LLM judges accept nonsense: baseline GPT-4.1-nano evaluator rating fell only 65 to 49 on nonsensical adversarial questions; agreement about 60% vs 70%.
agent_test: Test the scaffold's verifier on planted nonsense items.

claim: LLM sensemaking tools built on Pirolli-Card (not Weick) improve human exploration: Sensecape N=12, concepts 68.3 vs 22.8, t(11)=3.1 (re-checked); Selenite N=12, 840.3 s vs 1319.3 s, precision 98.8 vs 78.4 (re-checked).
agent_test: Not an agent test; use as design evidence for external concept structure only. Small N, within-subject, authors' own tools.
audit_note: Numbers verified (Sensecape 68.3 vs 22.8 t(11)=3.1; Selenite 840.3 vs 1319.3 s, precision 98.8 vs 78.4). Selenite's framing cites Pirolli and Card but also Dervin, Klein and others, so 'built on Pirolli-Card' is loose for Selenite; absence of Weick not checkable from truncated text.

claim: Hindsight-built training trajectories (path reconstructed backward) beat foresight data by 2.0% plan quality and are more diverse (SciSense, 3B-70B, 120K trajectories). Not re-opened.
agent_test: Retrospective reconstruction of a solved case as a few-shot exemplar vs forward exemplar. Gap pass: no evidence yet that hindsight helps at inference time; Kamoi says model-only feedback rarely works.

claim: Hindsight bias is the experimental cousin of Weick's retrospect; awareness does not remove it, considering alternatives does (secondary source only).
agent_test: After an outcome is revealed, ask the agent to rate what it would have said before; test alternatives step.

claim: Plausibility has a transition-based process account (Klein et al. 2023) with no experiment; the field lacks a quantitative test of Weick's plausibility property.
agent_test: Operationalise strain: count unexplained transitions in a story and test it as a trigger for re-framing.

claim: Cross-source sensemaking stays hard for LLMs even with retrieval (iAgentBench); reflection gave small or mixed gains.
agent_test: Run iAgentBench-style questions with and without a theme-linking operator at equal tokens.

claim: Organisational-AI field studies framed on Weick are small interview studies (7, 14, 23 focus groups); they show hands-on experience with AI limits gives realistic expectations.
agent_test: Not testable on an agent.

claim: Weick's Bhopal re-analysis could not be checked: only factual Wikipedia lines (two rival cause accounts; at least 3,787 deaths) were read.
agent_test: None.

claim: No clean enactment-vs-passive ablation at equal tokens exists. Closest: ReAct on PaLM-540B, HotpotQA EM Act 25.7, CoT 29.4, ReAct 27.4, CoT-SC to ReAct 34.2; ALFWorld best ReAct 71% vs Act 45%. Acting helps as a grounding check (CoT hallucination 56% of failures vs 0% for ReAct) but acting alone was below thought alone on HotpotQA.
agent_test: Arms at equal tokens: passive reasoning, probe-only, switch rule (probe when sample agreement is low).

claim: A second model instance as audience does not reliably cut plausibility drift: same-model debaters collapse to agreement (DCR up to 86.36%) and 2-agent decentralised debate adds about 0 to 1 point; a separate judge and 3 agents help (MMLU-Pro Qwen 66.46 single, 71.10 centralised).
agent_test: Reviewer with mandatory dissent, different model, vs same-model reviewer; measure flip-to-agreement rate.

claim: Self-judged validity (P(True), sample agreement) is a usable proxy trigger for a plausibility gap on a model trace; no one has tested Klein-style strain counts on traces. Evidence is from 2022-era models.
agent_test: Trigger re-framing when P(True) is below a threshold; compare to a fixed schedule at equal tokens.

claim: Columbia and El Faro show the same frame-lock shape as Mann Gulch (a prior or authority overrides repeated cues; further probes withdrawn or ignored), but no study measures cue-ignoring on a common scale. Sources are Wikipedia summaries of CAIB and NTSB reports.
agent_test: Vignette set with planted warning cues and a pressure line; count cues acknowledged vs dismissed.

claim: Maitlis 2005, Maitlis and Christianson 2014 (2,297 citations, 276 references) and Weick 1993 (3,637 citations) remain unread; counts of studies, four forms, and boundary conditions are unverified. No quantitative replication of HRO or Maitlis typology findings was confirmed (Vogus and Sutcliffe 2007 scale studies exist but were not read). One 2026 practitioner abstract claims 41% lower narrative alignment above 60% AI content (weak).
agent_test: None; research debt.
